Rashi on Chullin 27b:10:1.hebrew: מן היבשה - לפיכך יש לו חיות, בריא וחזק:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:10:1.english: From the dry land - Therefore it has vitality; it is healthy and strong.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:10:2.english: Raqaq - A swamp (garvila) that has both water and dry land:

Rashi on Chullin 27b:10:3.english: Know it - [That] they were created from the swamp mud.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:11:1.hebrew: ועוד שאלו - קונטריקון ההגמון את רבן גמליאל שאלות הרבה, והן בבכורות (דף ה.), וגם זאת שאלו. והכא תניי' משום גררא דעופות:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:11:1.english: And they further asked - The governor Kontarikon asked Rabban Gamliel many questions, and they are in Bekhorot (page 5a), and they also asked this. And here it is taught because of its connection to [the topic of] birds.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:11:2.hebrew: שרץ נפש חיה ועוף אלמא ממיא איתבריאו - עופות:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:11:2.english: "Swarming creatures, living souls, and birds" – evidently they were created from water - [This refers to] birds.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:12:1.hebrew: ולמה הביאן אל האדם - ר"ג קאמר לה, כלומר ולמה נכתבו כאן משום קריאת שם:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:12:1.english: And why did He bring them to Adam? - Rabban Gamliel said this; that is, why were they written here? Because of the giving of a name.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:12:2.hebrew: לקרות להם שם - והכי קאמר: ויצר מן האדמה כל חית השדה ואת כל עוף השמים, לראות מה יקרא לו, ולא איצירה קאי:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:12:2.english: To call them a name - And this is what [the verse] is saying: "And He formed from the earth every beast of the field and every bird of the heavens"; [the words] "to see what he would call it" do not refer to the forming.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:13:1.hebrew: משום דכתיב - "ואת כל עוף השמים", "על" – ויצר, דמשמע דאיצירה נמי קאי. לישנא אחרינא: משום דכתיב "על", כלומר, מקרא קמא גופיה משתמע דמן הארץ נבראו, דכתיב "על הארץ", דמשמע דמינה איתבריאו, וכתיב נמי בקרא בתרא "ויצר מן האדמה". זה שמעתי, וראשון נראה בעיני:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:13:1.english: Because it is written - "And every bird of the heavens," [and it says] "upon" [and] "formed," which implies that it also refers to the forming [of the birds from the earth]. Another explanation: Because it is written "upon" - that is, from the first verse itself it is implied that they were created from the earth, as it is written "upon the earth," which implies that they came into being from it; and it is also written in the latter verse, "And He formed from the ground." This I have heard, but the first [explanation] seems right to me:

Rashi on Chullin 27b:14:1.hebrew: אין שחיטה לעוף מן התורה - והיקשא דזאת תורת, לאקושי בהמה למליקת העוף, שתהא שחיטתה מן הצואר, כדאמרינן לעיל. ואפילו מתורה שבעל פה, מהלכה למשה מסיני, אין לו אלא מדברי סופרים. ואין נבלת עוף קרויה נבלה אלא אם כן מתה מאליה, או הרגה במכה שלא על ידי סימנים. אבל נחירה או עיקור סימנין כשר בו:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:14:1.english: There is no slaughter for a bird from the Torah - And the analogy of "this is the law" [is meant] to liken an animal to the pinching of a bird, so that its slaughter will be from the neck, as we said above. And even by the Oral Torah, as a halakha given to Moses at Sinai, it has only the status of a rabbinic law. And the carcass of a bird is called a neveila only if it died on its own, or if one killed it with a blow, not through the [severing of the] simanim (the windpipe and gullet). But nehira (stabbing the throat) or ikkur simanim (uprooting the simanim) is valid for it.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:15:1.hebrew: חיה נמי - דהא חיה נמי בהאי קרא כתיבא:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:15:1.english: Also a wild animal - For a wild animal too is written in this verse.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:15:2.hebrew: לפסולי המוקדשין - כדאמרינן לקמן בשמעתין: מקיש צבי ואיל לפסולי המוקדשין:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:15:2.english: To disqualified consecrated animals - As we say later in this passage: [the verse] equates the gazelle and the deer with disqualified consecrated animals.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:15:3.hebrew: איתקש לבהמה - ונימא: אין היקש למחצה:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:15:3.english: It was compared to an animal - But let us say: "There is no analogy [that applies] for only half."

Rashi on Chullin 27b:16:1.hebrew: דסליק מיניה - "או עוף אשר יאכל ושפך את דמו":
Rashi on Chullin 27b:16:1.english: That he had just finished discussing - [The verse:] "Or a bird that may be eaten, he shall pour out its blood."

Rashi on Chullin 27b:18:1.english: And it became an animal carcass in his hand - Unintentionally.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:18:2.english: One who tears out [the windpipe and gullet] or uproots [them] - Intentionally.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:18:3.hebrew: פטור מלכסות - דאשר יאכל כתיב (ויקרא יז):
Rashi on Chullin 27b:18:3.english: Exempt from covering - For it is written "that may be eaten" (Leviticus 17).

Rashi on Chullin 27b:18:4.hebrew: ליבעי כסוי - דהא כתיבא כסוי אנחירה דידיה, ומהיכי תיתי למיפטריה:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:18:4.english: Let it require covering - For covering is written regarding its neḥira (stabbing) itself, so why should we exempt him?

Rashi on Chullin 27b:18:5.hebrew: מי סברת בעוף - קאי בחיה. קאי דכסוי דידה, כי כתיב אהכשרה כתיב, והכשרה דידה שחיטה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:18:5.english: Did you think it refers to a bird? - It refers to a wild animal. It refers to the covering [of blood] of the wild animal, since [the verse] is written with regard to its fitness [for eating], and its fitness is slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:19:1.english: One who slaughters - [i.e., slaughters] something that requires covering [of its blood]:

Rashi on Chullin 27b:19:2.english: And he needs the blood - As [the baraita] explains:

Rashi on Chullin 27b:19:3.hebrew: חייב לכסות - על כרחו, ושוב לא יראה למלאכה:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:19:3.english: He is obligated to cover - Against his will, and [the blood] will no longer be seen for [use in] work.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:19:4.hebrew: כיצד עושה - להפטר מן הכסוי, נוחרו או עוקרו:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:19:4.english: How does he do it? - To be exempt from the covering [of the blood], [by] tearing (nochro) or uprooting (ikro) [the windpipe or gullet].

Rashi on Chullin 27b:1:1.hebrew: ופדר קמא למה לי - בשלמא ראש איצטריך לרבויי משום שכבר הותז, אלא הפדר למה לי?
Rashi on Chullin 27b:1:1.english: And the first "fat" (pheder), why do I need it? - It is understandable that the head needed to be included [in the requirement of covering the blood], because it had already been severed; but the fat (pheder), why do I need it?

Rashi on Chullin 27b:1:2.hebrew: דרך כבוד - שכשמקריב הראש, חופה הפדר על מקום חתך, מפני שמלוכלך בדם:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:1:2.english: A respectful manner - That when one offers the head [on the altar], the fat covers the place of the cut, because it is soiled with blood.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:2:1.hebrew: מייתי לה מהכא - שחיטה מן הצואר:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:2:1.english: He derives it from here - [That] slaughter [is] from the neck.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:2:2.hebrew: זאת תורת הבהמה - לעיל מיניה איירי בטומאת נבילות:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:2:2.english: This is the law of the animal - Immediately before this [verse], [the Torah] was discussing the impurity of carcasses.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:2:3.hebrew: עוף אינו מטמא במגע ובמשא - דכתיב "לטמאה בה", אין לך אלא מה שאמור בה "לא יאכל לטמאה בה":
Rashi on Chullin 27b:2:3.english: A bird does not transmit impurity through contact or carrying - For it is written "to become impure through it"; you have only what is stated regarding it: "He shall not eat it, to become impure through it."

Rashi on Chullin 27b:2:4.hebrew: בהמה אינה מטמאה בבית הבליעה - אם תחבה לו חברו. דתניא: יכול תהא נבלת בהמה מטמאה בבית הבליעה? ת"ל לא יאכל לטמאה - מי שאין לה טומאה אלא דרך אכילתה, יצתה זו שיש לה טומאה קודם שיאכלנו:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:2:4.english: An animal does not impart impurity in the place of swallowing - If his fellow shoved it into him. For it was taught in a baraita: One might think that the carcass of an animal would impart impurity in the place of swallowing; [therefore] the verse says (ת"ל), "[it shall not be eaten] to become impure by it" - [this refers to] that which has impurity only by way of its being eaten; this excludes [an animal carcass], which has impurity before one eats it:

Rashi on Chullin 27b:3:1.hebrew: מה בהמה בשחיטה - יוצאה מידי נבלה, דכתיב (ויקרא א) "ושחט את בן הבקר":
Rashi on Chullin 27b:3:1.english: Just as an animal, through slaughter - It is removed from the status of a carcass, as it is written (Leviticus 1): "And he shall slaughter the young bull."

Rashi on Chullin 27b:3:2.hebrew: אי מה בהמה ברוב שנים - מדאצטריך לעיל לרבות את הראש שכבר הותז, דאי בסימן אחד לאו הותז קריא ליה, ולא איצטריך לרבוייה:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:3:2.english: If so, just as [in the case of] an animal, [slaughter requires] most of two [signs] - Since it was necessary above to include [the case of] a head that was already severed: for if [only] one sign [was cut], it would not be called "severed," and there would be no need to include it.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:3:3.english: This - It is a limiting term:

Rashi on Chullin 27b:4:1.hebrew: מה עוף הכשרו מן הצואר - מליקתו:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:4:1.english: Just as with a bird, its fitness [for eating] is from the neck - Its *melika* (pinching the neck with the fingernail).

Rashi on Chullin 27b:4:2.hebrew: אף בהמה הכשרה מן הצואר - שחיטתה, והיינו דאמרן, ותנא מייתי לה מהכא:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:4:2.english: Also a kosher animal [is fit] from the neck - Its slaughter [is at the neck], and this is what we said [above], and the Tanna brings it from here.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:6:1.hebrew: זאת מאי עביד ליה - כיון דעוף לאו מבהמה יליף, אלא בהמה מעוף ילפא, מיעוטא מאי ניהו:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:6:1.english: What does he do with [the word] "this"? - Since a bird is not derived from an animal, but rather an animal is derived from a bird, what is the exclusion [implied by "this"]?

Rashi on Chullin 27b:6:2.hebrew: בסימן אחד - דכתיב בחטאת (ויקרא ה) "ולא יבדיל"; "זאת" ממעט: שלא לכל דבריהם הוקשו, אלא לדבר אחד:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:6:2.english: With one sign - For it is written regarding the sin-offering (Leviticus 5), "and he shall not divide it [asunder]"; the word "this" [in "this is the law of the animal and the bird"] excludes: They were not equated with each other in all their details, but only in one matter.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:7:1.hebrew: הבהמה והעוף - וכל נפש חיה הרומשת במים, דגים:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:7:1.english: The animal and the bird - [The verse continues:] "And every living creature that moves in the water" – these are fish.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:7:2.hebrew: לחייבו בשני סימנים - כבהמה, דנפקא לן ממנין לרבות את הראש שכבר הותז:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:7:2.english: To obligate him [to cut] two signs - As with an animal, which we derive from [the verse "Or" in] "from the count" [of the verse], to include the head that has already been severed.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:7:3.hebrew: אי אפשר שכבר הוקשו לדגים - דלאו בני שחיטה נינהו, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:7:3.english: It is impossible, since they were already compared to fish - For they are not subject to slaughter, as [the Gemara] says below.

Rashi on Chullin 27b:9:1.hebrew: הכא כתיבא אסיפה - דידהו אצל שחיטת בהמה, ומדשני בדיבוריה וכתיב בהו אסיפה, ש"מ דוקא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 27b:9:1.english: Here, gathering is written - Of the [fish], adjacent to the slaughter of an animal; and since [the verse] varies in its wording, and "gathering" is written with regard to them, we learn that it is specific.

Tosafot on Chullin 27b:10:1.hebrew: תדע שהרי יש להם קשקשת - תימה, מה צריך ראיה על זה, דקרא כתיב בהדיא "ישרצו המים שרץ נפש חיה ועוף"? וי"ל דמייתי ראיה, דכיון דבריאת המים ניכרת בהם, ראוי לדמותם לדגים לענין שחיטה:
Tosafot on Chullin 27b:10:1.english: Know [this], for they have scales - This is astonishing: why is a proof needed for this, when a verse explicitly states, "Let the waters swarm with swarming living creatures, and birds" (Genesis 1:20)? And one can answer that [the Gemara] brings a proof because, since the creation from water is evident in them, it is appropriate to liken them to fish with regard to slaughter:

Tosafot on Chullin 27b:11:1.hebrew: ועוד שאלו - פירוש קונטריקון, ההגמון את רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, ולא כמו שפירש בקונטרס את רבן גמליאל. ובכל דוכתי דאיכא ועוד שאלו, עליה קאי, ואע"ג דלא מייתי התם כמו בו ביום, שבכל הש"ס דהוי ביום שמינו בו את רבי אלעזר בן עזריה נשיא, כדאמרינן בפרק תפלת השחר (ברכות דף כח.):
Tosafot on Chullin 27b:11:1.english: And they further asked - Explanation of the Kuntrakon: [the one who asked was] the Hegemon, [and he asked] Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, and not as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres, [that he asked] Rabban Gamliel. And in every place where it says "and they further asked", it refers to that [same episode], even though it does not cite there "on that very day", [as is found] throughout the Talmud, that it was the day on which they appointed Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah as Nasi, as we say in the chapter [Tefillat HaShachar] (Berakhot 28a):

Tosafot on Chullin 27b:14:1.hebrew: בשפיכה בעלמא - ואפילו לר' מאיר דיליף לקמן בפרק כסוי הדם (חולין דף פה.) דשחיטה שאינה ראויה שמה שחיטה, דגמר שפיכה שפיכה משחוטי חוץ, מכל מקום אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו:
Tosafot on Chullin 27b:14:1.english: With mere pouring - And even according to R' Meir, who derives below in the chapter of Kisui HaDam (Chullin 85a) that a slaughter that is not fit is [nonetheless] called "slaughter," as he learns [by analogy] "pouring" (shefikhah) "pouring" from [the law of] those slaughtered outside [the Temple], nevertheless a verse does not depart from its plain meaning.

Tosafot on Chullin 27b:1:1.hebrew: ופדר קמא למאי אתא - מה שמקשינן, לכתוב חד ראש ותרי פדר, דמחד ראש ידעינן שהוא בכלל עריכה, ופדר קמא דדרשינן מיניה שחופהו על בית השחיטה ידעינן דראש קודם לכל אברים. נראה דאי לא כתיב אלא חד ראש, לא הוה דרשינן מיניה שכבר הותז, אלא הוה דרשינן [מיניה שחופהו על בית השחיטה, והוה שמעינן מיניה] שקודם לכל האברים; אבל השתא, מיתורא דכתיב ראש שני אשמועינן דשחיטה מן הצואר:
Tosafot on Chullin 27b:1:1.english: And what is the first "pader" (fat) needed for? - As for what we ask: [Why not] write one "head" and two "pader"? For from one "head" we would know that it is included in the arrangement (arikha), and from the first "pader," from which we derive that he covers it over the place of slaughter, we would know that the head comes before all the limbs. It seems that if only one "head" were written, we would not derive from it that it had already been severed; rather, we would derive [from it that he covers it over the place of slaughter, and we would learn from it] that it comes before all the limbs. But now, from the superfluity of the second "head" that is written, it teaches us that slaughter is from the neck:

Tosafot on Chullin 27b:2:1.hebrew: באיזו תורה שוותה בהמה לעוף - בפרק חטאת העוף בזבחים (דף סט:) דרשינן מינה: מה בהמה דבר שמכשירה לאכילה מטהר טרפתה מטומאתה, אף עוף כו'; תרתי שמע מינה:
Tosafot on Chullin 27b:2:1.english: By what teaching are an animal and a bird equated? - In the chapter "Chatat HaOf" in Zevachim (69b) we derive from it: Just as with an animal, that which renders it fit for eating (i.e., slaughter) purifies its terefah [carcass] from impurity, so too with a bird, etc.; we learn two things from it.

Tosafot on Chullin 27b:6:1.hebrew: מה עוף בסימן אחד - דכתיב "ומלק ולא יבדיל":
Tosafot on Chullin 27b:6:1.english: Just as [slaughtering] a bird [is valid] with one siman (organ) - For it is written, "and he shall wring [its head] but not divide [it]".

Tosafot on Chullin 27b:7:1.hebrew: דרש בר קפרא - לדידיה, איצטריך זאת לשום דרשא:
Tosafot on Chullin 27b:7:1.english: Bar Kappara expounded - According to him, [the word] "this" (zot) is needed for some [other] derivation.
